title: Predictive turn-bundling coordinator with horizon-based KV prefetch for streaming chat
creator: Anika Rao
description: Implement a coordinator that forms ephemeral bundles of streaming chat turns using a predictive horizon window. The coordinator will group turns from in-flight sessions into short-lived "bundles" when the model and KV cache predictions indicate overlapping KV slot access or contiguous token generation, enabling larger continuous batches without adding tail latency for actively typing users. The approach combines a short predictive horizon (50-300ms), per-session priority scores, and a progressive KV prefetch strategy that warms only the most-likely KV slots to stay within per-GPU slab budgets.
goals: Reduce p95 token latency for multi-turn streaming workloads by 8-15% relative to current slab-only allocation
Lower average per-token GPU memory footprint through selective KV prefetch (target 10-18% reduction)
Keep end-to-end additional jitter for single-turn, low-latency interactive clients under 25ms
Provide safe fallback to low-memory serving path when slab pressure exceeds 85%
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator integrated into serving runtime as opt-in flag and feature-gate
Bench dashboard shows p50/p95 improvements for representative streaming chat traces (internal dashboard link)
KV prefetch budget enforcement prevents OOMs under synthetic spike tests (load test PR)
Automated rollouts can throttle coordinator by route and customer tier via console

design_decisions: Horizon length: default 150ms with adaptive mode that scales 50-300ms based on active concurrency and recent typing signals
Affinity scoring: combine KV-slot overlap probability, recent-turn proximity, and session priority; weightings tunable via runtime config
KV prefetch policy: progressive prefetch of top-N predicted slots per bundle where N is derived from slab free bytes budget
Memory safety: soft reservations plus background reclaim using LRU-TTL and eviction callbacks to avoid blocking streaming paths
Fallback: if slab pressure > 85% coordinator reduces horizon to 0ms and disables prefetch for that GPU until pressure drops
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros: better batching efficiency and lower per-token cost for multi-turn flows, improved GPU utilization, fewer cold-KV fetches during generation
Cons: complexity in scheduler increases maintenance burden; predictive bundling may add jitter for single-turn low-latency clients if not carefully throttled
Risk: incorrect affinity predictions can cause wasted prefetches and transient memory spikes; mitigated by conservative budgets and rehearsal tests
Operational: need new telemetry and SLOs (bundle size distribution, prefetch hit rate) and console surface to toggle by customer
